confirmation.ordinary: Worker operations always use separate resolution and dispatch. A reversible manifest declaration never permits the shortcut. Return a challenge only for required material or effects; otherwise omit confirm.

request_card.rule: Show exactly the host's checked effect and its checked named inputs. Reject missing, duplicate, unchecked or altered display material. Derive decision and lifetime entries exclusively from offered actions. Reject their presence as material fields or duplicate offered decisions. A closed card supplies no decisions or lifetimes. The lifetime this_item is scoped to the exact checked item.

plugin_operation.destination_rule: When a checked execution-placement prompt supplies the destination, the host-written input:<placement slot> entry satisfies has_destination for that placement. Write it even if the slot is absent from material_inputs. Use the host label Machine and login and the checked option label as its value. A separate checked destination still requires destination. No other input entry satisfies this rule.

host.undo.rule: Only for a widening inverse. Include the host-written material in attempt_authority_end.actions.item_audience_widening. For other eligible inverses require no extra challenge.

confirmation.material_rule: Select the row by the checked operation and host surface. Check all material for the exact normalized request under the pinned context. Reject empty lists, duplicate names or missing required entries. For every current checked fact listed in when, require its entries with any substitution specified by that row. Include untouched prefills and all applicable material. Plugin challenges also include present manifest material_inputs as checked by the host. Host keys are host-owned. Every manifest input key is projected with manifest_input_prefix and its original local ID, using its declared label and checked value unless the row specifies host-written material for that input. The prefix is reserved for checked authored inputs, including host-resolved ones. It is unavailable to independent host entries. Render labels and checked values. Explicit default, none or clearing choices are shown with a readable label. The device cannot supply the challenge kind or facts.

cache_policy.persistent_row_scope: Start-anchored root list windows with invariant inputs only. Permit a literal collection and account-bound viewer:person. Deny search, references and route, form, selection or parent operands in source, filter or sort. Verify shape, host proof, account, space, template, Bind, signed scope_ref, offset, lifetime and opt-ins on write and load. On write the record must match the authenticated active view and reply, including own_space_member audience, scope_ref and window_ref. Index records on the device by the authenticated account, space and signed scope_ref so a scope invalidation can erase every offset without relying on the current viewport or lease. On load use only the matching local own-space root display. Never serialize a WindowResult.
cache_policy.persistent_row_authority: Display on unlocked devices as unconfirmed until the host confirms or corrects the rows. Encrypt with account- and space-bound keys. Never persist guest or public rows, action credentials or contexts. Apply device_reconciliation at next authenticated contact and at local sign-out. Erase on account switch or known revocation. Apply persistent_row_invalidation to every authenticated invalidation. Every action requires a fresh host context. Body-derived parts require the matching offline grant. Apply offline_download retention.
cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation: For every accepted authenticated invalidation, durably erase all persisted row records in the exact invalidated scope, including all cached offsets and records no longer displayed or written under earlier leases. A renewal omission identifies the scope through the exact requested result that was invalidated. Stop queued writes from invalidated results and prevent those records from prepainting after a restart. Complete or recover pending erasures before reading cached rows on launch. Apply erasure even if the invalidation has no reason and arrives without a separate revocation notice. Only a fresh authorized result may write replacement records. Preserve records in unrelated scopes.

execution_attempt_authority.principal: A distinct host-minted principal per exact attempt, bound to the sender and the admitted request. Its separately fenced lease grants no ordinary invocation ticket or member principal.
execution_attempt_authority.broker: Use purpose-specific operations on admitted host-issued refs within effect ceilings and the discovery grant below. Reject raw enumeration and bulk exports, foreign scopes, forged tickets, and job enqueue, ticket minting or delegation used to widen discovery.
execution_attempt_authority.renewal_and_egress: Recheck the exact attempt and runtime fence, the sender's live authority, grants, job or session, package generation and placement at renewal, effects and output egress. Revoke fences immediately and stops renewal.

discovery.grant: The sender's request to find items grants discovery within that space. No separate confirmation in either Full access or Approve for me. Existing controls still apply to any later effect.
discovery.authority: Apply the file audience rule before matching, ranking, counting or returning rows, fields and excerpts. Keep the existing query bounds and access records. Recheck live authority at planning and delivery. A child stays under every ancestor's ceiling.

file_audience.sender_only: Use the sender's full scoped live read rights.
file_audience.shared: Require the sender and every authorized file reader to have access to each discovery input.
file_audience.in_flight: Apply attempt_authority_end.actions.item_audience_widening on audience expansion. On loss of discovery source rights suppress affected pending output before delivery or commit. Resume the work only in a fresh attempt that excludes ineligible context.

item_policy.declaration: A kind may declare attempt_discovery:item_policy. Carry a host-owned creator_only or consent_only fact on each item of that kind. Unknown state defaults to consent_only, including imports with no trusted authorship provenance. A package cannot use its participant metadata as authority.
item_policy.write: Default to consent_only. On a checked create by and for the authenticated creator, the host may set creator_only if authorship is checked under the authorship rule and there is no admitted other participant or writer. Read-only membership does not constitute participation. For a creator_only item, apply opaque_writes to any body change, including a body-and-rename save. Before admitting another participant or writer, commit the protective state in the same authority transaction. A people conversation uses consent_only. Do not admit other participants until that exchange is pinned. This rule is the same in personal and shared spaces.

authorship.rule: The installed write_origins declaration opts into a checked middle source. For an attested write, the host composes the prefix, the exact middle selected under host_input or attempt_output (or empty for a recorded-span deletion), and the suffix under item_engine.attested_write. Attribute framing to the owning package and the captured middle to the acting person, or to their exact attempt for output. The attempt starter is the person used for item discovery. Neither framing nor this attribution supplies per-message consent or proof of who originally composed submitted prose.
authorship.host_input: At checked dispatch, capture the declared host_input operation input from its verified binding to a host-owned composer or editor text field and the exact user submission for that component. A matching string received through an arbitrary operation argument, literal, prefill, file picker or import path supplies no evidence. Before dispatch bind the captured text to the operation and package generation, item or checked create scope, acting account and request. A checked job may inherit that captured source only when admitted by that invocation for the same item and actor. The attested source kind input selects this existing capture, without sending its bytes back to the host. Recheck the bound source for the exact write. An editor import, bulk paste or raw whole-file replacement path is opaque even when the editor normally supports checked text. Text pasted into a message composer is a submitted message. The host cannot establish its original author from the text.
authorship.attempt_output: Resolve the declared attempt_output top-level text field on validated committed contribution output, using the exact live attempt started by the acting person and its pinned call and output sequence. Source kind output names that sequence; take the middle directly from the committed field, without accepting bytes from the worker. Only output already delivered to the owning job under that call is eligible. Attribute verified output to the starter for discovery. Plugin-assembled text, other attempts, stdout before validation and arbitrary tool or imported bytes are opaque. No worker-supplied actor or input-origin flag can qualify a write.

cases.own_prompt: The host composes the creator's checked input in its own append. The middle and the bounded package framing preserve existing creator_only eligibility, including when the exact admitted job inherits the capture.
cases.own_agent_reply: The middle is the exact validated contribution output of the creator's live attempt. The composed append preserves existing creator_only eligibility.
cases.other_participant: The middle is the checked submission of another participant. Attribute the middle to that participant and apply consent_only to the item.
cases.import_or_unproven_write: Raw bodies and opaque appends, including imports and staged plugin-built files, set or retain consent_only even in the same invocation with the marker omitted.

item_policy.read: Before list, search, direct body, metadata or file reads, or derivative retrieval, exclude consent_only items from attempt discovery. Check the same rule before matching or deriving titles, excerpts, scores, counts, order, fetch refs or any output, including through another query or child attempt. A creator_only item remains discoverable by attempts acting for that same person under current sender-only or shared-audience checks and other ordinary grants. No other actor's attempt gains access through the creator_only state. A consent_only selection may go only through attempt_disclosure, never through discovery.
item_policy.opaque_writes: On create, save or append, including staged publication, an authorized writer may request consent_only. The host also sets it if the new content belongs to someone other than the sole creator or has unproven authorship under that rule. Otherwise preserve the existing state. Commit protection with the authority or body change and fence old attempt reads, pending derived output and their projections before the new head or grant is visible. Omission of the marker cannot bypass the check. The host alone may clear it under clear.
item_policy.clear: Only the host can clear the marker. Under the item and authority fence it must prove checked sole-creator content and eligibility, including the absence of another admitted participant or writer. It must also ensure older protected revisions and derivatives remain excluded from attempt reads, search and cached projection. Then publish the checked fact and its projection together. No editor, package, import, ordinary save or Undo can clear it or restore an older clear value. If the host lacks that proof, keep the marker set. No general recertification operation is enabled in the first slice.

provider_login.custody: Mount only manifest-declared paths from the authorized binding for the space type. Reject escaping paths, symlinks and overlapping mount paths. Check the binding, its live approval, exact build and eligible placement at admission, reattachment and renewal. Fence access and affected work on binding revocation or replacement under attempt_authority_end.actions.grant_change. Keep login data out of unrelated accounts and spaces, output, backups and other mounts.
provider_login.personal_space: Only mount the backing directories the acting person approved for this harness in their eligible personal sandbox. Each declared path maps to private backing storage for the harness by default, even when another harness declares the same path. Share backing storage only when the person explicitly chooses the harnesses and exact directories. A name or declaration confers no access. If the target file has other readers, using a personal login or changing permission mode cannot enable tools. The selected-material call in attempt_disclosure requires a separately qualified boundary and remains unavailable until qualified.
provider_login.shared_space: The space Owner approves the shared login. The Owner or a Manager configures that approved login for the space. The binding has separate space-scoped backing storage and pins the space, declared directory set and exact installed harness build, including package, entry and image digests. A build or directory change requires fresh Owner approval. Use this binding by default in a shared space. Allow a member's personal override only when explicitly selected under execution_placement. If the harness needs a login and the selected binding is ineligible, refuse execution without falling back to another login. Keep tools off for both choices under owner decision 74 until qualification proves a boundary that protects the login from tools and other runs. Apply attempt_authority_end.actions.item_audience_widening before a personal run's item gains another file reader. Admit a shared execution only when the placement also keeps incompatible saved sessions out of reach. The disclosed-attempt case in attempt_disclosure requires tools and an eligible qualified boundary. Refuse that case until the boundary is qualified.
provider_login.disclosure: At install disclose the publisher, image digest, placement, mounted item-data scope, each declared login directory and approved network egress. Explain that program code and tools in the person's own sandbox can read and transmit available login data. At shared login setup show the space and pinned harness build, that eligible space members' runs use the configured login, and the recorded notice that a personal subscription is licensed to one person.

harness_placement.approval: Use the host's recorded approval for the exact reviewed build, pinned to the installed package, harness entry and image digests. Review the build once. A different build needs its own approval for hosted placement. Apply the same approval checks to bundled and community harnesses.
harness_placement.approved: Allow any eligible placement, including hosted sandboxes. Check current placement, profile, actor and effect authority at admission, reattachment and renewal.
harness_placement.unapproved: Installation is allowed. Admit execution only on a machine enrolled by the authenticated acting person. Recheck that enrollment at admission, reattachment and renewal.
harness_placement.disclosure: The install screen says which placement rule applies and discloses network access and access to the person's provider logins when granted. A publisher mark or a package declaration cannot establish reviewed-build approval.

carrier.invoke_scope: Dispatch to the exact admitted package, digest, epoch and ticket. Stamp protected job and alarm metadata as in HostWorkerInvokeFrame. Refuse worker-origin invoke or worker-supplied host metadata.
carrier.author_context: The host stamps request_id, stable actor and authored_at once on admission and replays the same values, including jobs, alarms and contribution calls. Expose these plus checked job and alarm metadata only, without raw tickets or mutable machine data. Use the stable request ID as the namespace for caller-chosen subeffect keys; scope receipts to the originating authority, method and exact target and material. Equal subeffect keys replay and changed material conflicts. Authored time is not a live deadline. The optional actor_label is pinned to the already checked destination audience. If the audience is unresolved, omit it. An item writer must recheck that audience before using the label in a readable path.
carrier.callback_scope: Check direction, epoch, package digest and exact live invocation ticket before reading declared method input. A callback ID is local to the invocation and pairs with exactly one host reply; mismatched or late IDs produce no delivery or effect. Reply uses the checked method output or safe status and code. Complete is terminal; validate data or the declared park schema and saved checkpoint before the existing atomic park. Keep chunk progress ephemeral. Cancel fences first; ready uses the host-issued startup ticket and exact checked package and epoch, before any invocation. Neither side accepts author, job or alarm metadata from the worker. Carrier credit and fence control remain independent of callbacks.

execution_placement.source: Any app may declare a choice prompt with options.host:execution_placement for a single-item execution action, including its composer's Send action. Permit one placement slot per action. Resolve the live member, target item and action from the activation context. Validate the supplied HarnessRef against the installed contribution, requested item and activation's app and scope under the extension and placement rules. Read the eligible binding inventory on the host without waking a plugin. When that action also declares a harness extension choice, the submitted option must resolve to the same HarnessRef before dispatch.
execution_placement.options: In a shared space put its eligible configured space binding first and mark it default. Also offer the acting member's own live enrolled machines paired with their own eligible approved login for this harness, in an isolated sandbox. In a personal space use the same enrollment and login options and the established eligible personal default when configured, including eligible hosted placement. Never offer another person's enrollment or login. Filter by live grants, exact build, enrollment, profile and placement eligibility before paging. If the activation is for selected-material disclosure, apply attempt_disclosure.placement before offering choices. Use the existing 50-option cap and an opaque next cursor pinned to the same authorized option set. Labels identify the machine and whose login will be used, using safe profile display names where needed. Omit default_ref if there is no eligible default. Only the first page can name a default, and it must equal a ref in that page's options.
execution_placement.request_and_submit: The authenticated renderer calls choice.options with the checked context, placement slot, selected HarnessRef and the activation_id it will use for resolve. Request another page with the returned next cursor, if present. Render only the host labels and default. Submit the selected ChoiceRef under that slot in ResolveActivation.interaction.choices, with the same activation ID and context. When the slot is declared this ref is required, including when accepting the returned default. A shared-space personal choice requires explicit selection for this run and is never the default. With no selected eligible option, the action stays unavailable. Discard options and cursors on context or harness change, lease loss or disconnect and fetch fresh options. Reject stale or foreign choices and return to the picker without dispatch.
execution_placement.dispatch: Bind each choice to the actor, space, lease, action, slot, activation ID, item, harness build, exact machine and login binding. Pin the selected choice when resolving activation and recheck at dispatch. Give the checked worker operation only the opaque ChoiceRef as that named input. Forward it as ExecutionJobStart.placement with the same harness on the same checked dispatch, including an authorized contribution invoked under its checked scope. Require the exact ref when that activation supplied one. Reject a ref from any other input, invocation or receipt. Consume it once when admitting the job, bind the resolved placement to the receipt and allow exact replay. Never grant a plugin access to option labels, cursors, enrollment IDs, login identity or paths through this exchange. Protected preview material, when required, uses the host label and is renderer-only.
execution_placement.default_and_fence: For a job admitted without a placement slot and for a scheduled alarm use the applicable eligible default under provider_login. Refuse a missing or stale checked choice without substituting a default. Recheck the pinned binding at admission, promotion, claim, reattachment and renewal. Do not silently fall back if a pinned binding loses eligibility. Shared runs, including a personal override, use whole-file-audience discovery and the shared tools rule. An override uses only the acting member's isolated sandbox and login. No unrelated run can use that login via this choice. For a selected-material invocation use the placement restriction in attempt_disclosure; the ordinary shared personal override does not apply to that invocation.

start_job.description: This request is for the execution arm of start_job. Its job ID resolves one installed declaration. Ordinary jobs refuse harness and placement. Apply admission and provider_login.

execution_intents.admission: Only a declared replayable job with execution:true and a checked live item whose installed kind declares execution_target. Keep one eligible head job or active attempt per item. The successor rule governs queued jobs. Pin the audience generation, actor, job, package, exact harness binding, selected placement and profile, and effect ceiling. Apply execution_recovery.update_fence before admission or launch. Use the top-level ExecutionJobStart.harness or the already-pinned alarm binding. Apply execution_placement to the StartJob placement operand. Never select a harness or placement from opaque job input. Under the lifecycle fence refuse deleted, archived or retired targets. Reserve quotas once. Exact replay returns the current receipt without another admission. Refuse changed operands under the same receipt. Recheck the same bindings at promotion and claim, without substitution. No caller-supplied host job context. Apply initiating_installation and target_operand. Apply extension_points.calls.preflight before issuing an admission receipt.
execution_intents.initiating_installation: For an interactive execution, pin the authenticated initiating device installation in host-owned admission state. Recheck its ownership, validity, generation and expiry at admission, promotion, claim, reattachment, renewal and effect or egress authorization. Loss of a view lease or transport alone does not retire work. An autonomous alarm uses its own pinned alarm principal. Apply session_or_job_retirement on loss of the installation, including for the exact queued successor and descendants; unrelated authorized work remains live.
execution_intents.stop_and_archive: Idle archive excludes unresolved execution jobs, live attempts and protected approvals. Protected archive pins the entire affected set, including head and successor. Stop pins its exact target and any affected descendants. Both apply attempt_authority_end.retirement_authority. Never retarget a replacement.
execution_intents.successor: The existing checked start_job may admit one durable FIFO successor per item while its head job or attempt is active. A queued successor has a receipt and no execution lease. Promote it only after the head is terminal and its attempt authority and teardown are settled. Recheck item, actor, grants, pinned harness, placement, profile and quota at promotion. Replay the receipt without adding a job. At capacity refuse with pending_limit. Stop pins the exact target. Archive, widening and revocation fence any affected queued jobs before publishing the authority change. One item never has two running attempts.
execution_intents.target_operand: ExecutionJobStart and targeted AlarmSet name the checked item once, in top-level item. Resolve the installed run operation and its single-item target.field. Reject an input that supplies that field, even if equal; require live authority on the top-level item and exact declared kind. The host injects the checked item into that field before validating and dispatching the run input. HostWorkerInvokeFrame.message.job_context.item for execution jobs corroborates the same target and conveys no independent authority. Replay, promotion and claim reconstruct only from the pinned target. For an untargeted ordinary alarm, omit item and require a target-free run operation.

execution_recovery.submissions: The renderer records a submitted Send, follow-up, steer or Stop in its encrypted account- and space-scoped outbox before transmission, including the activation ID, intended action, checked target as a portable locator, and submitted values. A queued control also records the old exact attempt or intent identity as a non-authorizing ref. When renewing the action context for an absent control receipt, compare it with the newly eligible execution.control target. Retry only with the same exact target. If the target is gone, settle the control as stale without any effect on another attempt. Store no lease, challenge proof or placement secret. On reconnect authenticate and use activation.receipt to recover a lost ACK. Replay only that same activation with freshly authorized context and any required confirmation if no receipt exists. Bind the receipt to actor, space, exact action, target and normalized input and recheck before returning it. Changed operands refuse under the same ID. An uncertain or expired receipt never becomes an automatic fresh Send. Erase unauthorized entries on revoke or sign-out. While the update fence is held or startup admission recovery is in progress, commit the checked input, request ID, order and pending outcome into the durable queue before ACK, or leave it in the device outbox until authenticated admission is available. Keep one logical submission across the device, job and attempt. Loss of a receipt ACK cannot duplicate prompts, successor admissions or provider starts.
execution_recovery.controls: Keep a bounded durable delivery ledger for the exact attempt. Check the complete encoded UTF-8 steer delivery including LF under control_limits before admitting it. A steer appends its request ID, checked text, sequence and target before reply. Stop atomically commits its attempt or pending-job fence, logical outcome and any outstanding remote delivery. Reserve one Stop slot independently of the steer budget. On reconnect dispatch an outstanding Stop for its old exact attempt before any delivery or renewed effects for it. An old target already terminal acknowledges stale; never retarget a successor. Retire undelivered steers on Stop, authority loss or attempt completion. Preserve outstanding deliveries and their deduplication records until settled, then apply the ordinary receipt retention period. A plugin may explicitly queue an undelivered steer as a new submission only after proof it was not applied. The harness records deduplicated acceptance and reconciles actual application by exact request ID. Transport ACK is not effect ACK. If a provider lacks proof for ambiguous delivery, do not blindly reissue. Such a harness cannot pass the exactly-once gate.
execution_recovery.reattach: Persist enrollment, machine boot, runtime reservation, exact attempt, call, build, effect fence and committed cursor before starting. Reconnect on the enrolled carrier with fresh proof of the same execution and contiguous immutable log, bound to the current authenticated session and one-use host challenge. Recheck actor, job and current scope, stop state and placement before fresh renewal or egress. Do not expose proof to the renderer. A forged or foreign proof has no effect. Accept same-run continuation only with live proof. An exact recorded terminal can settle and publish that old call after verification without granting further harness execution. A new boot, an unproven execution or an uncertain effect follows failed_reattachment. Retain committed output. A fresh continuation is a choice of the owning plugin using execution_session_bind and current authority, independent of automatic reattachment. After failed continuity it requires a new request from the authorized person. Do not start it as an implicit replay.
execution_recovery.machine_log: The harness owns the durable working log on its enrolled machine. Commit immutable ordered output records and the terminal there before acknowledging producer acceptance. Relay only a bounded window from the last contiguous host-durable acknowledgement; the working log is the buffer. Server or carrier absence has no time limit of its own and drops no output. The run retains its own deadline and disk and execution quotas. On quota exhaustion apply the ordinary visible run limit after retaining the terminal and all accepted output. Charge durable unacknowledged bytes to that run and keep them through reconnect until accepted or durably retired by Stop or another authority fence. Never evict unacknowledged output to make room. Replaying a previously accepted position neither reruns the harness nor republishes an item effect. The host acknowledges contiguous durable commits only on the checked call and carrier generation. The relay ignores stale epoch acknowledgements. The owning job appends with the existing call-and-sequence receipt.
execution_recovery.outage_authority: Transport loss alone does not close an intact enrolled attempt or its already authorized inference path. Keep the machine-local supervisor, containment and own run deadline. Park host-mediated effects, tool approvals and any new operation that needs live host authority until the server reauthorizes it. Do not grant new destinations, credentials or broker capabilities while disconnected. A host revoke fences server effects and delivery at commit and queues the exact Stop for the first reachable machine connection. Verified local containment loss still freezes and tears down the runtime. The absence of authenticated host renewals by itself does not arm teardown on this enrolled recovery path.

update_fence.surface: Authenticated local operator socket. Expose no per-space names, job IDs or output.
update_fence.rule: Report recovering until startup reconstructs admission and live execution state. Idle means no admitted start, running, reconnecting, frozen, stopping or unsettled accepted execution work remains. Future alarms are not admitted starts. Observe is advisory and reports held while an update fence is held. Acquire atomically compares the execution count and outstanding admission transitions with idle and closes execution admission before returning held. Keep a lightweight admission permit through the transition, with no host-wide lock across storage work. While held, pin new checked execution submissions durably as queued, without an execution capacity reservation or launch. Expose the queued exact intent to the authorized Stop control and allow its durable cancellation before admission. Alarms, children, promotion and claim cannot start execution past the fence. Ordinary authorization and queue limits still apply. Release only on successful restart recovery or after at most max_seconds from the original grant. Retry does not extend the fence or acquire it again after release. On release deliver queued work once in original scoped order under live admission checks. A forced update does not wait for or acquire an idle fence and relies on exact reattachment.

attempt_authority_end.retirement_authority: In addition to the action's own live authority, an actor-initiated action that retires jobs or attempts requires the actor to be the starter of every affected job and attempt, including any queued successor and affected descendants, or to hold current PluginsManage over every affected scope. Resolve and pin the entire set at admission, including for confirmation. Recompute it and recheck authority under the lifecycle fence in the commit that retires work. An unauthorized target refuses the whole action before effects. Require a fresh resolution and confirmation where applicable if the set changes. Mandatory safety fencing on authority loss or runtime failure uses its own fence rule and proceeds independently of starter consent.
attempt_authority_end.commit_rule: Make the local fence and the specific recovery work durable before reporting success or allowing any later admission, renewal, effect or egress. Invalidate queued dispatch and scoped references and fence descendants. Where authority spans databases, durably fence affected spaces before publishing the authority change and block work until reconciled. Keep the exact attempt identity, generation and cleanup key. Dispatch no remote work under the fence. Recover committed cleanup after crash before reply or dispatch. Deduplicate remote teardown by exact attempt, and release quota only after verifying it. Earlier committed effects stay committed.

archive.before_reply: Apply retirement_authority. Fence every affected exact attempt and durably refuse every affected pending job, including head and successor. Commit the archived head, any eligible Undo and deduplicated cleanup with those fences in one FULL transaction on the per-space content writer. Its durable authority rows are decisive for admission, replay, claim, renewal and egress; a jobs database notification or projection cannot authorize work independently. Undo leaves those fences and refusals in place.
archive.after_commit: Exact-attempt Stop and bounded subtree cleanup. Pending intent without an attempt needs no remote Stop.

stop.before_reply: Fence every affected exact attempt, durably refuse any affected pending intent, and store the Stop receipt and deduplicated cleanup under the same lifecycle commit. The scoped Stop never cancels an independent successor.
stop.after_commit: Exact-attempt Stop and verified subtree cleanup.

space_erasure.before_reply: Space admission tombstone and recovery-visible authority fence for every affected attempt, descendant and unresolved intent. Record cleanup before acknowledging erasure.
space_erasure.after_commit: Stop affected attempts and reclaim space data only after verified teardown.

account_erasure.before_reply: Account principal fence and a durable affected-space fence before publishing erasure. Retire that principal's attempts, descendants and pending intents. Hold affected spaces closed until reconciliation.
account_erasure.after_commit: Stop affected exact attempts and finish account cleanup after teardown.

membership_revocation.before_reply: Live membership generation and a durable affected-space fence for attempts, descendants and unresolved intents whose authority disappears.
membership_revocation.after_commit: Stop only attempts that lose their authority and reconcile scope cleanup.

grant_change.before_reply: Changed effective grant or profile generation and a durable fence for attempts, descendants and intents whose admitted authority no longer holds. A widening grants no additional attempt rights.
grant_change.after_commit: Stop affected exact attempts and reconcile the grant or credential references.

item_audience_widening.applies_when: Apply when an authorized change adds a file reader to an item with recorded widening protection or a bound personal-authority job, attempt or saved session. Resolve direct and inherited file access under the existing fence. A title-only grant adds no file reader.

instances.lifecycle_and_other_grants: Any restore, unarchive, Undo, grant, membership or policy change that newly activates file-body access, including by inheritance. Scope the rule by the authority change, regardless of which surface makes it.

material.name: file_disclosure
material.label: File sharing
material.value: The new readers can read the whole committed file, including anything the agent found or wrote using your own access.

confirmation.rules: Require host confirmation by an authorized sharer. Show the checked target or scope, new audience and permission with the host-written file disclosure. Bind the confirmation to the effective change. Recheck it under the authority fence and require fresh confirmation if the checked change differs. This overrides ordinary Undo and full-swipe shortcuts. For invitations, require sharer confirmation of the covered grant at issue and matching confirmed scope at either redemption path. A redeemer cannot supply the sharer's confirmation.
confirmation.committed_text: Publish access to the entire committed file, including transcripts. The sharer decides whether to disclose it. Do not scan records for source eligibility or refuse because the file contains personal discoveries. Attachment bytes retain independent delivery checks.

item_audience_widening.before_reply: Before the wider grant is visible, durably fence every exact attempt in the affected item with personal-only authority (full-rights discovery or tools with a personal native login). Retire affected personal-context intents and descendant authority and durably discard uncommitted output, including anything staged or queued for delivery. Pin the committed file boundary and persist deduplicated cleanup. Fence other pending derived output if the wider audience cannot read its sources. Use the commit_rule for changes that span databases. In the same durable authority change retire all incompatible saved ExecutionSessionRefs, including completed sessions. Derive retirement from the checked item and audience generation without parsing files or contacting the placement.
item_audience_widening.after_commit: Dispatch idempotent exact-attempt Stop and verify teardown. Later attempts use the shared discovery and tools rules. Do not carry forward discarded personal attempt context or reattach a fenced attempt. Only a new admission using committed file bytes and context cleared for the new audience may run in the widened scope. The placement must keep retired personal sessions unreadable even by raw path or provider session ID.
item_audience_widening.item_record: Record widening protection on the item in the commit of its first file or snapshot write by or on behalf of a personal-authority run. The host owns this durable item fact. Preserve it across package updates, disable and uninstall, and across item revisions and restore.

item_erasure.before_reply: Persist item deletion or purge and fence affected jobs, attempts, descendants and saved bindings. Trashing an item with an active attempt requires an authorized Stop first.
item_erasure.after_commit: Stop affected live attempts on the authorized erase path, verify teardown and finish bounded purge.

session_or_job_retirement.before_reply: Persist session or alarm-principal invalidation or cancellation or replacement of exact jobs, with all affected attempt, descendant and intent fences. Interactive installation revocation or expiry is mandatory safety fencing for its exact jobs, including a queued successor, and their descendants. Use commit_rule if the installation and work span databases. Do not retire other installations or unrelated jobs. Apply retirement_authority to actor-initiated retirement of jobs, independently of mandatory authority-loss fencing.
session_or_job_retirement.after_commit: Stop the affected attempts and retire their queued work.

package_or_placement_retirement.before_reply: Invalidated package generation, enrollment, placement or runtime lease and durable fences for its affected attempts and intents.
package_or_placement_retirement.after_commit: Dispatch exact Stops where reachable and reconcile runtime teardown before releasing quota.

failed_reattachment.before_reply: Under the lifecycle fence durably retire the exact old attempt and its descendant authorities with the interrupted status, committed file boundary and deduplicated cleanup. Apply when same-execution proof, continuity, safe provider continuation or fresh renewal fails while the attempt may still exist. Refuse later renewals even when its placement lease is valid.
failed_reattachment.after_commit: Dispatch exact old-attempt Stop or reconcile verified death. Preserve published records and reconcile any uncertain provider effect before an authorized person can request a fresh job.

ancestor_authority_loss.before_reply: Persist the lost ancestor fence and its subtree admission and effect fence, including descendant attempts and checked child reservations, before completing the authority change.
ancestor_authority_loss.after_commit: Stop affected descendants by exact attempt and retire the affected child reservations after verification.

runtime_freeze.before_reply: Persist the attempt generation and arm independent runtime deadlines before admission. At a qualifying local containment or authority cutoff close the gateway, fence queued dispatch and freeze the full subtree. Apply execution_recovery.outage_authority to an intact enrolled runtime during transport loss. Freeze blocks effects and egress while hold and quota remain.
runtime_freeze.after_commit: Dispatch no Stop on a mere freeze. Thaw only after fresh same-execution proof and one-use renewal. Failed recovery or elapsed teardown deadline follows its own retirement row.

runtime_teardown_deadline.before_reply: The durably armed recovery deadline starts local teardown independently of the host. On observation persist irreversible retirement for that exact attempt and its subtree. No thaw once teardown starts. Keep quota while death or gateway closure is unverified.
runtime_teardown_deadline.after_commit: Reconcile runtime-local kill and verify subtree and gateway teardown. Reclaim quota and retire the private spool only under its recovery policy. No new remote Stop is needed for the runtime-owned teardown.

attempt_terminal.before_reply: Persist the exact attempt's terminal or interrupted state, fence its scoped work and descendants, and record cleanup and spool retirement. This includes verified process termination and a reached run deadline or quota. On the enrolled recovery path, a stalled relay waits on the durable working log instead of marking the run failed.
attempt_terminal.after_commit: Verify teardown of remaining workers, tools and gateway, stopping the exact attempt if needed. Preserve the committed file boundary and uncertain-effect reconciliation.

application_cutover_requirements.deployment: Qualify a fresh install. The owner permits a fresh redeploy of this project's production installation and data at the Threads cutover, with the old Calternal app and its userdata outside scope. Legacy session migration, historical attribution proof, old-file parity and calternal-thread/v1 import are not gates. Use additive migrations and the running-release upgrade check for every change merged before cutover.
notes: History browser over revisions created on the fresh install.
threads: Attach and reopen files through a generic upload and checked item refs.
Provide queued follow-ups through plugin-owned state and jobs.
Qualify the §8 product wake gates and remove native first-party handling at cutover.

extension_points.resolve: An app declares versioned extension points and interface schemas in its installed manifest. Resolve the qualified owner package and app, point, version and contribution kind; pin both package generations and validated signatures. A contribution references an operation owned by the contributing package. Require an exact point version in the first slice. The paired input schemas and paired output schemas must match as parsed JSON values, including the resolved targets of offline schema references. Object order and formatting do not affect equality. Do not attempt semantic equivalence. Validate inputs and outputs against both declarations at use. A local app ID alone makes no global namespace claim. Dispatch operation IDs and their used prefixes remain globally exclusive, including existing host and bundled reservations. Reject conflicts without replacing the live owner. App descriptions attach contributions through ExtensionUse. At each use require the matching contribution kind and declared operation.
extension_points.authority: Show the relationship, requested data and effects at install. Both packages must be enabled and the contribution selected by the app or viewer as applicable. Invoke through the broker with the caller's checked rights intersected with the approved declarations and live item and field grants. No direct package-to-package sockets, automatic rights, undeclared UI injection or access to the other package's files.
extension_points.rows: Publish the basic indexed row without a wake. Resolve optional fields only for visible rows, coalesce work, and deliver only for the same checked source ref, lease, audience and revision. Failures omit that field. If an app uses a list entry with a checked source ref, maintain visibility by source authority before pagination or counts. A personal entry grants no rights on its source.
extension_points.files: Use item_engine.format_open. Editor contributions declare eligible format IDs and versions. The person can explicitly select one without changing the owning format's default. Fall back to an eligible read-only view when preservation or write compatibility is unavailable.
extension_points.harnesses: Images and entry assets are pinned. Only an admitted execution job may invoke a selected harness contribution. Use identical placement, signature, native-profile, authority and disclosure checks for bundled and community code. An app may publish another harness interface. There is no bundled namespace owner.

choices.rule: Only the owning app or its checked device interface can request choices. Bind the short-lived option to the exact declared point and scope. For an eligible harness option also issue the durable HarnessRef. Reuse the binding for the same exact tuple. Limit stored bindings to the installed contribution inventory and retire them when their pinned digests or enrollment lose eligibility. Recheck membership, placement, publisher approval, installed contribution, digest, point and profile at each job or alarm claim. Refuse a stale ref instead of substituting another build. Receipt replay never reissues or widens authority. A worker request cannot assert renderer context, issue renderer refs or reuse its pagination cursor on the renderer route.
choices.renderer: The renderer requests extension.choices using its app and the exact prompt slot declared as options.extension with the point ID. Option refs and the continuation are scoped to the active authenticated view, lease, actor, checked action, slot, declared point and installed generations. For harness choices return both ref and harness_ref. The renderer uses harness_ref to fetch placement, but submits the picked option ref under its slot in ResolveActivation.interaction.choices. Resolve it at activation to the same checked HarnessRef, and supply that typed ref as the operation's named input. Other extension choices resolve to their scoped opaque contribution refs. Recheck choices at dispatch. Discard dependent placement options on harness change. If both choices are present, require that the resolved harness equals the placement's pinned harness before dispatch. Never accept a raw contribution ID or renderer-supplied HarnessRef as the submitted choice.

contribution_call.scope: The owning checked job may start one pinned contribution per admitted attempt. Resolve the checked point, installed contributor and exact attempt from its ticket. Validate input against both declared interfaces and apply authority and disclosure before starting the entry. Resolve an existing receipt first; exact replay returns the same call without invoking the contributor again. Require the exact checked contribution_input from admission under preflight.

contribution_read.scope: Only the owning job with live exact attempt and checked call may read the bounded committed suffix after the last consumed sequence. Omit after for the first read. An empty batch means no committed suffix yet. Use a bounded wait on the same call or resume by checked job checkpoint. Never issue a second invocation to poll output.

calls.output: Validate output data against both declared output schemas. Number outward frames from seq 1 in the machine log under the exact checked call. The host accepts a contiguous sequence and durably commits it before acknowledging it and fences further output on cancellation, revocation, replacement or wrong attempt. Replay by exact call and producer sequence or refuse changed input. Apply calls.limits to each full ContributionCall, ContributionEntryInvoke and ContributionFrame: count UTF-8 encoded JSON including field names, escapes, sequence and terminal fields and one LF. Count the LF even inside a broker envelope; that envelope also has its own bound. The host spool bounds the unconsumed relay window including its reserved terminal. Apply execution_recovery.machine_log for durable output while disconnected. When the window is full, pause relay and keep the machine log. Return credit as the owning job consumes the committed prefix. If input would exceed the bound, refuse contribution_frame_limit before launching the entry. One exact terminal frame follows its last output. A link loss is not an entry exit. An observed exit with neither verified terminal nor continuity proof is interrupted. Apply encoded-byte and frame budgets from calls.limits before accepting new producer output. Limit each bucket to one second of burst and do not refill it on reconnect. The machine meters producer admission and records exhaustion as an ordinary quota terminal with reserved capacity. Host and relay pace catch-up under the same host ingest limits, using credit and bounded reads. A temporarily full host window or ingest budget delays replay of accepted records and never turns them into an output failure. Replays of already accepted positions consume no additional durable admission. Keep active cursors and pending receipts for as long as their work remains unsettled. Apply the existing receipt lifetime after completion. Closing a consumer does not rerun the provider.
calls.commit: The contributor may write only its own eligible files and can return a portable locator for an independently authorized file. The calling owner reads committed frames and writes its own item using the exact live attempt fence and stable subeffect receipts keyed by call and sequence. An ok producer terminal seals output but the attempt remains fenced and eligible only for the owner's checked publication until the owning job completes; only then publish execution completion. Stop, revocation or failed recovery ends that authority immediately. Preserve already committed owner effects and the contributor's committed log. If a live owner retries after lost append ACK, replay that receipt without calling the entry again. Bind the owning job's writer ticket to this exact attempt. Replay can rebind only after validating the same admitted attempt and its publication fence.
calls.preflight: Before persisting an execution job or accepting an execution alarm, validate and pin the exact contribution_input and selected installed interface. Check its UTF-8 JSON encoding under calls.limits for both full ContributionCall and ContributionEntryInvoke, including LF. Use exact encoding for known fields and safe encoded maxima for fields assigned later, including request, attempt and call refs. Return broker status 413 with code contribution_frame_limit if either envelope could exceed the cap. No job, alarm, launch or prompt write follows that refusal. An action that submits a contribution and saves the initiating prompt admits first. Its owning job may save that prompt only after the successful admission receipt and under the live writer fence. Deliver the pinned input in ExecutionJobContext, and require the later contribution_call input to equal it under the receipt comparison. Recheck interface, authority and exact frame bytes at launch. A worker cannot substitute or expand the input after preflight.

harness_abi.entry: Run the verified digest-pinned executable entry at a fixed read-only mount with one UTF-8 newline-delimited JSON ContributionEntryInvoke on stdin. Deliver checked inputs only. Read one JSON ContributionFrame at a time on stdout; validate sequence, output schema, bounds and terminal. Broker-issued authority for declared own-file effects uses the attempt channel, never the stdout stream. Diagnostics are bounded, scrubbed and distinct from output. No session or login bytes on either frame. For entry callbacks use harness_abi.broker. Never provide another package's item writer.

broker.rule: The trusted machine relay exposes a private AF_UNIX stream in the exact attempt sandbox only. The entry opens one stream and writes one UTF-8 JSON call plus LF per frame; the relay returns one JSON reply plus LF for each checked callback ID. The relay stamps the live call, attempt, build, epoch and ticket from its own binding. The entry sees only the checked call and reply payloads. Reject forged metadata and undeclared methods. Reuse checked carrier callback scope, the contributor's own-file authorization and effect receipts. Close and fence on authority loss before any subsequent effect or reply; do not move this authority to another attempt or a network endpoint.

harness_abi.image: Acquire only from the declared OCI source at the pinned digest or from a verified operator-provisioned local copy. Verify the image digest and reviewed build identity before placement, never fall back to a name or tag. Verify the packaged entry bytes against their asset pin at build, install and launch. Mount only the selected approved login paths and expose no shared file-tree mount. Stop or cancellation fences the channel first and tears down the entire existing supervised subtree. Expose the verified entry as executable inside the sandbox regardless of archive file mode. harness.image_source is an HTTPS OCI registry repository without a tag or digest; combine it with the separately pinned image digest. Disclose the normalized source at install, or that the image is operator-provisioned. Recheck and approve a changed source before use.
harness_abi.egress: Apply the contribution's explicit execution network declaration to the placement independently of the ordinary worker. Default none. Disclose publisher, image digest, entry, mount scope, placement and approved execution egress using the same approval path for all publishers. Read harness.execution_network, independent of the worker's network declaration. Normalize and approve the requested destinations under the existing network rules. A contribution or worker grant cannot widen it. Enforce the separately approved execution policy at placement and on egress; recheck and fence a narrowed or revoked policy.

extension_points.identity: The host stamps the logical ContributionIdentity from the installed manifest into the owning job's checked context and into its eligible extension options. The app may keep it as a participant identity. A package must not recycle a contribution ID for a different logical agent within that package. Do not resolve or launch from this stored identity alone. A fresh host choice and exact reviewed build, publisher, grant and live binding checks still apply; no auto-rebinding on an identity or display label match.

alarms.admission: Only a declared replayable alarm job. Bind the pending alarm to a package generation, creator, checked target and due time. Protect replacement and cancellation by live authority and request receipt. Consume and admit exactly one durable job in the same recovery-visible transaction; delivery or restart replay can only replay that job. Resolve the installed job declaration. Require the top-level AlarmSet.harness operand for execution:true and refuse it otherwise. It is the sole harness operand. Never select a harness from the opaque job input. Resolve and pin that durable HarnessRef for the exact actor, space and target at alarm set. At due-job admission and claim, re-resolve the same binding and place it in the protected ExecutionJobContext. If it is ineligible, admit no execution and never substitute a harness. Execution alarms use the applicable default login binding and cannot opt in to a personal placement in a shared space. Replacement is a new checked admission; receipt replay preserves the exact binding. Apply execution_intents.target_operand at set, admission and claim. An execution alarm requires item as well as harness. Require contribution_input for execution alarms and refuse it for other alarm jobs. Apply extension_points.calls.preflight before accepting or replacing the alarm. Recheck the same pinned input when admitting its execution job.
alarms.late: An eligible missed alarm is still delivered once at durable job admission. The host stamps scheduled_at, actual_at and missed into that receipt and replays them unchanged. Pin the effective grace at alarm admission, using AlarmSet.grace_seconds or its single schema default when omitted. missed is true only when actual_at is strictly later than scheduled_at plus the pinned grace. Equality is on time. This measures admitted delay, including a slow queue, rather than inferring an outage. The plugin decides whether to skip and computes its next time.
alarms.disable: Persist retirement of pending alarms and fence admitted work when the package is disabled, uninstalled or loses authority. A later enablement does not recreate retired alarms.

file_append.rule: A kind declaring append_file: true has one append stream per item, addressed by the ordinary item and revision for both append and range reads. Check write authority and exact expected revision, plus live execution and audience fence when the writer is attempt-scoped. Commit the bytes, revision, byte boundary and receipt recoverably before ACK. Use checked staging and outbox recovery. Preserve the previous readable range pin until revoke, purge or expiry. Reject conflicting receipt fingerprints. Apply item_engine.attested_write to the attested alternative and the item discovery policy to opaque bytes.

publish.scope: Apply view_snapshots.body_content and the write checks in view_snapshots.authority. No live view invocation may publish.

view_snapshots.authority: Treat the snapshot as plugin-authored item content. The package's declared reads and the acting principal's live read grants bound the inputs, as when writing the item file. Only a run of the installed kind owner with live item-write authority can publish or replace the retained snapshot, normally the run that wrote the file. Check write authority when minting the publish scope and again under the commit fence. Bind publication to actor, package generation, item, slot, exact source revision and the host-derived item audience. Validate the native description. Deliver a retained snapshot only to its bound audience under view_snapshots.body_content.
view_snapshots.state: Store and serve only the newest page for a snapshot slot without a wake. Mark a still-authorized snapshot stale after a head advance. A valid writer publication replaces the slot and invalidates the corresponding open view. Show loading with the basic item shell if absent. Evict retained views within the byte caps and reclaim superseded generations.
view_snapshots.retention: Regenerable appdata. Apply view_snapshots.body_content on revoke, purge or generation retirement and reclaim in bounded work. No backup dependency. A snapshot is never authoritative or the only copy. It contains no host chrome, confirmation UI, live actions, external frames, automatic network loads or bearer tokens. Inline links use item_views_entries.content. Store checked asset identities instead of delivery refs.

context.scope: Publish only. Mint the exact host-derived scope for an installed kind owner's write-authorized run. Deny it on the live view path. Apply view_snapshots.body_content.

view_snapshots.live_view: On a separate live item_view.open request, the declared refresh read operation receives ItemViewRead and returns ItemViewPage for the requesting member only, with state:live. Scope it to the exact viewer, lease, item and checked source revision. Hold the retained view while the refresh runs only as permitted by view_snapshots.body_content. The admitted call may wake the package under the existing runtime rules. Apply pending and payload bounds. Keep its output transient and apply view_snapshots.body_content. A refresh cannot mint or redeem a publish scope or change the retained snapshot, even for a viewer who can edit. Guest and public requests use retained content only and never invoke refresh.
view_snapshots.body_content: Item views are body content, whether retained, stale or live. Every production and delivery path uses the same live revision-specific body-read check as a file read for that exact item and source revision. Check the acting principal at production admission and again before committing or returning produced content. Check the viewer at open admission and immediately before delivery. Title access alone is insufficient. On a relevant invalidation, fence outstanding delivery and invalidate affected results on the authenticated lease. Close the lease if the host cannot signal invalidation. Clear displayed and buffered content on relevant invalidation, lease loss or disconnect, and ignore superseded replies. Apply view_result_retention on renewal. With no authorized result, show the basic item shell.
view_snapshots.paging: A snapshot holds the newest page and optionally its private older boundary. An authorized member can request older pages through item_view.open with live:true and the issued cursor. Bind each external cursor to its checked viewer, view, item, slot, source revision, and plugin boundary. Resolve and reauthorize the exact pinned revision before invoking the owner. No offset or count. Absence of older ends the chain. Do not mix revisions in one chain. The plugin supplies older pages when awake, under admitted wake rules. Guest and public views receive the retained newest page alone. Meter each page against the snapshot bounds.
view_snapshots.follow: The cursorless latest live page supplies a follow ref to its eligible active member. On a committed item change send changed on the authenticated subscription so the renderer requests the latest live head without a cursor. Keep still-authorized pages while refreshing, then replace the chain if the pinned revision changed. On body or asset authority loss, purge, retired source or other relevant invalidation send invalidated and apply body_content before any further output. Bind and fence the follow ref with the result and lease. Keep one follow per open item-view slot under the existing per-view subscription cap. Coalesce signals and meter them with the existing live update cap. Apply subscription_catch_up to report an authorized advance after the followed revision. An enabled refresh slot can return a readable empty-file page with a follow ref before the attempt emits its first output.
view_snapshots.assets: Accept only checked immutable image and attachment references at publish or refresh. Bind them to the item-view source, verified asset revision and audience. Omit an inaccessible leaf and its metadata. On delivery mint a scoped ItemViewAssetRef and check both the item body authority and the asset's independent live access again at every range open and delivery. Fence on source or asset revoke. Serve normalized still PNG or JPEG images with at most 512 KiB and 2,048 pixels on either edge. Attachments use the existing file limits and checked ranges. Each response is at most 64 KiB decoded. Treat labels and author lines as plain authored data.
view_snapshots.anchored_open: The renderer resolves a portable locator, then opens the checked item view with live:true and the opaque anchor instead of cursor. Resolve one authorized source revision under body_content. The owning reader selects the page containing that anchored leaf and echoes the exact anchor; verify the leaf is present once. The same bounds and older continuation apply. On absent, unreadable or unknown anchor disclose no anchor result or body; use opaque refusal for item access and anchor_unavailable only for an already readable item. An anchored page is not the live head and has no follow ref. Stamp only app-owned anchor values; the renderer can copy a locator plus anchor as a link.

viewer_item_state.storage: One private record keyed by space, item, installed owner and acting account, shared by declared viewer fields, draft slots and read positions. It survives restart and device changes. Omit absent declared values. Keep at most 16 declared scalars and one 4,096 UTF-8-byte draft per item and account per declared multiline slot, with at most four slots. The host validates Text (4,096 UTF-8 bytes), finite Number, Boolean and canonical Timestamp against the declaration. Install rejects clashes with shared and generic field IDs and incompatible reuse of a slot. Drop when the item/account is purged or the plugin is uninstalled. Invalidate delivery on loss of membership or item access.
viewer_item_state.authority: Only a current signed-in member with live item access may read or mutate their own state. A declared owning-plugin operation for that acting person may call viewer_state_read or viewer_state_write under the same check. Derive the actor from the admitted interactive invocation. No overrides, impersonation, unattended jobs, requests from another plugin, guest or public viewer, cross-view aggregation or shared-file writes. A read-only item may still accept its own read position, but never a composer send or edit. Draft writes additionally require current send or edit authority. After revoke, omit the values and clear affected device rows, drafts and private contexts.
viewer_item_state.write: Use one row compare-and-set with a version and checked request receipt. For declared fields, null clears the value. Host-maintained reading positions and drafts use the same store and are unavailable to a declared field patch. Refuse writes to fields with a declared entry count source. Reject unknown fields or cross-type updates. A draft's declared slot may project its plain own-account preview through an explicitly declared private Text field whose ID equals the slot. Keep only the latest value for that slot and cap its preview by the field budget.
viewer_item_state.bind: Fields carry viewer_self. A ready authorized member projection may use them in fields, marks, conditions, filters and sorts through the actor's scoped index. Apply the window replay/loading and plan gates. Do not expose their presence or values in other viewers' projections, totals, rank, exports, logs, offline download, and persisted shared or device row records. An absent field contributes no value. Qualify a rejected unsupported_plan rather than scanning.
viewer_item_state.qualification: Use two members, a guest and two devices. Check independent values and order for a shared item, stale compare-and-set, replay, purge and revoke during read and index publication. Updating one person's fields must change no result, count or activity for any other viewer. Restart and verify persisted private state.

item_views_entries.entries: Use immutable recorded spans at one checked source revision. Validate each entry anchor and order against the owning app's checked item revision and span/anchor index. Check live body access at admission and delivery. The owning writer may declare an item-local entry_anchor on ItemCreate or ItemAppend. Bind it once to the new recorded span and immutable order in the same commit as that span. A replace keeps the anchor and order, with deletion retiring it. Replays return the original binding and collisions fail before effects. Read entry associations from that index. Retire affected index entries with the opaque-write fence. Entry display names, edited_at, asked_by and pending state are application content; grouping keys are opaque within this item and cannot establish identity. Author ownership and distinctive contribution marks are host projections obtained from ItemRecordedSpan origins and the verified provider mark policy. Do not infer identity from display names or accept a plugin-supplied claim of viewer ownership. One entry owns at most one quote. Apply ordinary item-view node/depth/byte and worker frame caps to the aggregate page, checked details included.
item_views_entries.content: Inline markup is limited to emphasis, strong text, code spans and explicit http(s) links. It uses plain text leaves, with no HTML, scripts, embeds, images, URL previews or implicit fetch. Item links use SnapshotLink with ItemLocator, through item.locate and its independent authorize-on-open check. Render an unavailable target without leaking a title. Quote nodes must match a checked quote dependency of that exact entry at its page revision. Use only the host-projected quote text, checked source and optional authorized author and jump target. Omit the quote when access or deletion is fenced. Never accept plugin-supplied quote display text. Date and system markers are display leaves. Render an unread separator from the checked first_unread anchor and own count, with no authored marker carrying private data.
item_views_entries.access: The host derives item-view access and reason from the live item grant, lifecycle and common-group policy. Emit the checked access state for entry views, with read_only reason lapsed, archived, trashed or grant as applicable. Names of groups and cause details are private. Gate mutation controls, admission and commit on the result. A read-only result may still show permitted read actions and body content. No actions, private reading, request cards or activity on ready or stale retained pages. Never persist the private live overlays with a shared snapshot.
item_views_entries.actions: Entry actions are installed item-view configuration with at most eight NonSwipeInvoke entries, scope and optional own_only or age conditions. No live actions from arbitrary page content. The host offers action contexts only for exact checked anchors in the delivered live page and for eligible viewer, read/write mode and scoped policy. {entry:anchor} resolves to the host-issued EntryHandle for that exact record, with item, revision, actor, lease, component and action bound. The host pins the resolved entry in confirmation and rechecks live policy, own condition, host-calculated age and head at dispatch and effect commit. A forged or stale context returns no operand or effect. Entry refs never authorize cross-item or bulk row use.
item_views_entries.reading: Only an opted-in member item view uses reading state. Store the last visible acknowledged entry in viewer_item_state, with a monotonic ordinal from the checked record order so edits above it do not move it. On item_view.read require an entry actually delivered in this live chain. Update only the acting reader and return the current own version. Derive first_unread from the next authorized retained entry. Require config.reading to name the declared own Number field with source entry_unread and optionally entry_mentions. Project counts from the checked entry order after the actor’s marker, excluding retired entries and the actor’s own person-authored entries. Record recipient mentions from the checked composer ChoiceRefs on that entry commit, without parsing the text or trusting a plugin-supplied recipient. Count mention matches for that actor only. Use qualified scoped bounded seeks and maintained counts; never scan older content or enumerate the readership on entry save. If these plans are not qualified or the projection is catching up, omit counts and mention targets. The marker is the only per-person write for this projection. item_view.open position unread, latest or mention takes the checked live target or latest when unread has no target. A missing mention target returns anchor_unavailable. If a saved anchor is gone, seek the nearest surviving successor by immutable order. Older and anchored pages continue from their checked cursor. Register follow before reading both head and reader state. On catch-up compare both independent scoped versions. A reader_state signal refreshes only the original member and scoped view, leaves still-authorized content mounted, and never discloses private activity to other readers.
item_views_entries.selection: An opted-in live member item view may choose one entry or a contiguous range of at most 128. Check both anchors, one item, revision, lease and component, and every intervening authorized entry in recorded order. Both endpoints must come from delivered pages in the same chain. A single-mode request omits last. Mint the existing opaque SelectionRef scoped to this entry selection, accepted only by a matching {entry:selection} action through interaction.selection_ref. Reconsider all selected refs and grants before material disclosure or effect, and refuse a stale head before delivering bytes. Author-by-author grants under attempt_disclosure remain required for a called-in attempt. Selection alone is not consent.
item_views_entries.request_cards: The host may insert at most eight live RequestCardRecord overlays keyed by an exact delivered entry anchor. Only the currently designated consenting author receives the card. A scope or recipient change invalidates it. Use the existing request resolve action, checked material and resolution context. Consent-specific requests bind exact selected entries, requester and receiving attempt and offer deny or the allowed once/this_item lifetime. Include expires_at for a one-minute request deadline; the host owns the actual timeout and withheld entries. Do not draw a card from a plugin-supplied request payload or infer a grant from a renderer choice. Keep actual disclosure off until per-author consent and revoke exchanges qualify.
item_views_entries.composer: Use FormNode.entry_context to bind the checked item-view component. A successful checked entry action can set then.composer and return an EntryComposerRef, with one form and reply or edit mode tied to the actor, entry, revision and lease. Use entry_composer.open for the mode and checked edit prefill. Recheck authority, editable scope and current revision on submit. {entry:composer} resolves exactly that context, with no raw source supplied by the renderer. Keep personal drafts in viewer_item_state and clear only the submitted version on ok, preserving concurrently updated drafts. A condition reads a declared earlier field in the same scoped form with exists or typed equality. Hidden fields and prompt slots supply no inputs, refs, defaults, uploads or required errors. Host recomputes conditions on captured data before preflight and confirmation. Refuse forward dependencies, cycles and cross-form conditions. Item-participant mentions page from live checked item grants and admitted contribution associations only. Return ChoiceRefs from that exact field; accept at most 16 matching choices in interaction.mention_choices and resolve to checked account or contribution operands with the submitted plain text. No group or directory search. Disable mention and consent workflows until the underlying participant grants qualify.
item_views_entries.attach: One checked file form field accepts at most eight AttachmentRefs. Begin checks declared byte length and hash and returns the current permitted size limit, expiry and a private scoped stage. A chunk accepts at most 64 KiB decoded, contiguous offsets and replay with the same bytes. A finish verifies exact length and digest and returns a checked ref visible only to the uploader in that item and field until a verified-write activation consumes it. Bind accepted refs to the committed item revision in the same publication intent. Check upload, submit, source and delivery authority separately. Use existing storage-tier and quota limits, retire abandoned stages by deadline and refuse foreign, expired or changed content. No raw path or uploaded body in the action envelope.
item_views_entries.activity: Optional live-only activity lists at most 16 labels and a host-stamped expiry of at most 30 seconds. Show working and consulting only from authorized active job status. Typing delivery needs a separately qualified authenticated source. No retained view, file, journal or history entry for activity.
item_views_entries.qualification: Require cold display without private controls, scoped entry contexts and safe inline parsing, filtered quotes and deleted-source races, same-author grouping across older pages, exact single/range rejection on stale head, viewer-only state across devices, draft compare-and-set across a successful Send, hidden prompt operand refusal, forged participant and file refs, and one consent answer only from its designated actor. Attach and queued follow-ups still gate a fresh install.

offline_download.authority: Authenticate a member's device and mint a host-signed account, device, space, authority-scope manifest of currently readable item revisions and attachments. Read each ref in bounded chunks with the same live grants, revision and device binding. Do not bundle provider profiles, secrets, scratch or protected activation material. The signature uses Ed25519 and a distinct calternal-offline-download-v2 domain over canonical JSON without proof, pinned to the authenticated host. For row display, match offline_grant to the verified manifest's signed grant_ref and exact source and field. Apply device_reconciliation to that ref independently of the row scope.
offline_download.retention: No offline expiry by default. The authorized space owner may configure an expiry under OfflinePolicy. Encrypt device-local bytes and derivatives at rest. Erase expired grants and dependent data locally. Apply device_reconciliation for next-contact revocation and local sign-out, including cached derivatives, views, indexes and keys. Future bytes are fenced immediately. A disconnected device or an exported copy cannot be erased remotely.
offline_download.row_projections: Body-derived display parts may persist for a live member whose signed offline grant covers the exact source and field. Ordinary template and row cache entries remain display only; never restore authority tokens.
offline_download.selection: Pin one grant_ref to the checked selection, snapshot of eligible source revisions and authority checkpoint. Bound the explicit selector, manifest page and range read independently. There is no total offline inventory or selection cap from this exchange. All_readable advances through the authorized space inventory in bounded manifest pages with the same grant_ref, including attachments in further pages as needed. Continue by checked cursor; verify each page and use its signed grant_ref for every dependent local part. Stop an invalidated selection rather than substituting different revisions or a new grant mid-download.
