Keep restart-safe authority evidence for a grant across all its pages so reconciliation can check its continuity within the per-page work bound, without replaying or reading the selection. A relevant authority change in any page invalidates the entire grant if continuity cannot be proven. A device can request a fresh selection under current authority.

trash.scope: One Trash per space for all item kinds.
trash.rule: Authorize each read, restore and purge against the item and space. Purge in bounded background work while packages sleep. An inverse that adds file readers applies the common audience widening action. Start retention at trash commit. No item kind or package overrides the retention period.

view_result_retention.rule: Host windows, plugin search pages and stored or live item-view pages use the same result_versions and retained_results exchange. On a successful renewal with an unchanged grant revision, re-confirm the exact result ref and version, current audience and checked scope, including the active settle generation for a plugin search, the slot for an item view, and live access to each exact item, asset, quote dependency and source revision represented in the result. Retain each still-authorized unchanged result by acknowledging the exact pair, without rerendering or invoking a plugin. Treat a changed or refused result as an invalidation of that result only. A changed audience requires a new view. Apply subscription_catch_up to each retained subscription and its result check.
view_result_retention.scope: Retain only on the same authenticated view, account and cache partition. Rebind the acknowledged result's eligible continuation, follow and item-view asset refs to the renewed lease. Asset reads still apply view_snapshots.assets at admission and delivery. Supply current scoped contexts in retained_results for retained plugin-search pages. Entry actions and composer contexts must be rebound or unavailable on renewal. Keep unchanged content while opening the live entry overlays under the renewed lease. An old entry, selection or composer ref may not cross a scope loss. A missing context is unavailable. Replace old tokens as a set. Invalidate selections or activities whose originating result or context no longer holds. Acknowledge each exact result at most once under the existing aggregate cap. Reuse the recorded window scope_ref for an unchanged checked scope, and use the exact omitted result's scope for persisted row erasure.
view_result_retention.renderer: Keep confirmed content on screen. Clear the affected result on actual invalidation, lease loss or disconnect. On a fresh authorized view retry a missing item page from its head and re-settle any missing plugin search chain before requesting its first page. An acknowledged unchanged chain continues from its retained cursor without another settle. Resume a partial chain only from a retained boundary; discard a dependent suffix without that boundary. Ignore replies from superseded requests.

subscription_catch_up.scope: Apply this order to the live renderer subscriptions for item-view follow, window pushes, default and explicit profile search, and view open or renewal. One-shot reads do not open subscriptions.
order: Register the authorized scoped subscription first. Make its registration effective against publication before reading the baseline. On renewal keep the watch active while rebinding or register its replacement first, with no gap.

Read the current committed revision or published result watermark of that exact authorized scope. Compare it to the revision or result the viewer held when registering, opening or renewing. With no previous result, use this read for the initial reply.

Deliver any newer authorized state or the route's invalidation or changed signal. Merge notifications queued during the read with catch-up, coalescing duplicates by the same scoped revision order. Never let an older snapshot overwrite a later result and never miss a publication racing registration, catch-up or the first reply.
subscription_catch_up.authority: Keep scope and version order server-side. Do not compare opaque refs lexically or infer visible changes from a space-wide watermark. Recheck the exact lease, audience and live authority before delivery. Fence superseded scopes, preserve each route's loading, invalidation and coalescing rules, and do not wake a plugin to perform catch-up or reconfirm unchanged results. A scoped invalidation may identify a result the host had issued to this lease after access to its content is revoked. It must carry no revoked content or new scope metadata. Fence outstanding deliveries for the invalidated result before signaling and keep live pushes and invalidations ordered with rebind. Close the affected lease if an invalidation cannot be delivered. Each accepted invalidation applies cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation to its named scope, whether or not that scope is still displayed.

item_view_follow.scope: The active authenticated lease and the follow ref identify one exact checked item, slot, source revision and audience, including that live head's page chain.
item_view_follow.delivery: Use changed for a newer authorized head, reader_state for newer authorized overlays under item_views_entries, and invalidated for a relevant invalidation under view_snapshots.follow. On changed fetch the newest live head and replace the old page chain when its revision changes.
item_view_follow.clears: On invalidated clear the affected displayed and buffered item-view pages, asset refs and bytes, older cursors, follow ref, activity, entry contexts, selections, cards and composer prefills. Apply cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation. Item-view subscriptions issue no persisted row records. Keep the rest of the view.

window_pushes.scope: The active authenticated lease and the issued scope_ref identify the exact Bind scope and checked route operands. Only touch that scope even if the same Bind now shows another collection.
window_pushes.delivery: Push the newer authorized window of the current live Bind scope. When affected displayed data cannot remain visible, invalidate even if a replacement window is still loading. Omit settle_generation.
window_pushes.clears: On invalidation clear the exact Bind scope's windows, count, displayed cache and assets, selections and action contexts, including buffered data and dependent activities. Erase all persisted row records for that scope_ref under cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation. Apply immediately during held keys. Discard superseded outstanding replies and request the viewport again under live authority. Keep other scopes.

default_search.scope: The active authenticated lease, issued scope_ref and settle_generation identify the exact checked search scope. Match any parent and Bind to the issued scope.
default_search.delivery: Use the same window signals with the active settle_generation. Echo the parent for a per-parent search. A scoped invalidation also discards earlier provisional search rows.
default_search.clears: Clear as for window pushes, for this exact scope_ref and settle generation only, including provisional rows and the displayed count. Apply cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation. Search scopes issue no persisted row records. Keep other scopes.

plugin_search.scope: Match the explicit lease_ref, Bind and settle_generation; a settled generation pins one exact query and checked route, parent and profile scope.
plugin_search.delivery: Use the same invalidation on an authorized advance that supersedes the chain or on loss of its authority. Fence the cursor chain and its derived contexts before delivering the signal. No unsolicited page and no worker wake. Ignore a signal for an old lease, Bind or settle_generation.
plugin_search.clears: Clear the exact chain's displayed and buffered pages, continuations, selections including set refs, and action contexts. Ignore in-flight pages for the invalidated generation. Apply cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation. Plugin search issues no persisted row records. Keep the rest of the view. To search again, settle with a fresh generation under live authority and request the first page.

renewal.scope: Match request_lease_ref, renewal_id and cache_partition. Match each retained pair or omitted pair to the exact requested window_ref and result_version, then to its recorded scope. A replacement host window carries its own scope_ref. Post-renewal signals must match the renewed lease and their own scope keys.
renewal.delivery: Return replacement host windows and exact retained pairs in the matching renewal reply. Omission of a requested exact result from retained_results invalidates that result. Put eligible catch-up windows in that reply or send the watch-specific signals under the renewed lease after the reply. Fence old-lease signals at handoff. Carry a pending invalidation for a previously issued window scope across handoff under the renewed lease. Emit it before any replacement results for that scope and omit that scope from retained_results and windows in the renewal reply. Item-view and plugin-search content arrives only through their ordinary read routes.
renewal.clears: Clear unacknowledged results and dependent selections, contexts, assets or continuations under view_result_retention. For each invalidated result erase any persisted row records of its recorded scope under cache_policy.persistent_row_invalidation. Keep exact retained results and their replacement contexts. On lease failure or disconnect clear all live content of that view under the existing lease rule.

device_reconciliation.contact: On every authenticated device reconnect or new authenticated session, start device.reconcile immediately in parallel with cold display and live view opening. Use one logical reconciliation for this host, account and device across all spaces, independent of open views and leases. Take a stable local inventory of held scope refs and offline grant refs, including closed apps and spaces. Erase protected data without a verifiable inventory ref. Send unique opaque refs in bounded pages, with no rows, item IDs, bodies, proofs or filenames. There is no total inventory cap. Send one page at a time in order, starting at zero and marking the final page with last:true. An empty inventory uses one empty final page. Every non-final page carries at least one ref. Fresh live reads and writes can proceed. Stage new protected disk acquisitions outside the prepaint inventory until the current reconciliation completes.
device_reconciliation.validity: Return only subsets of the current page's submitted refs. Resolve each ref under the live authenticated account and device across its eligible spaces. A scope ref is valid only for an eligible persisted-row scope with proven continuity of the persisted row authority generation, including row and field authority. A query still being readable is insufficient if any held rows could have lost authority. Retain enough bounded authority evidence to check this after closed views and restart, or omit an unverifiable ref. An offline grant is valid only for its exact signed device binding with proven authority continuity for the whole covered selection and live space policy, using offline_download.selection. No unbounded selection walk on the reconciliation path. Omit an unknown, foreign, revoked, expired or unverifiable ref without a reason. Recheck validity before reply; never treat this exchange as authority for a live effect.
device_reconciliation.apply: On each accepted page, durably erase each omitted scope's row records and each omitted grant's bytes, keys and dependent views, indexes and row display parts, even if the enclosing row scope remains valid. Repaint the affected display as the answer is applied. Leave refs waiting for later pages alone. Reject a returned ref not on the submitted page. A known local invalidation or erasure always wins over a positive reply. Fence buffered writes for erased refs and complete or recover erasure before any later disk prepaint. Mark the new inventory complete only after the final matching page and durable erasures for every accepted page. Interrupted attempts leave the last completed inventory minus committed erasures. Never restore erased refs on retry.
device_reconciliation.sign_out: Signing out is local terminal reconciliation with an empty surviving inventory. Retire the active reconciliation ID before accepting any further reply. Close the display gate and durably erase all row records, offline grants and their dependent data and keys for the signed-out account on this device before sign-out completes. Do it even if the host is unreachable. Resume any interrupted local erasure before later disk prepaint.
device_reconciliation.attempt: Use a fresh reconciliation_id for every attempt, including retries, on the current authenticated device connection. Retire the previous ID before sending a replacement and restart paging from zero against the remaining held inventory. Accept only the reply from the current authenticated connection that echoes the active ID and pending page and last flag. Ignore delayed, duplicate and retired replies. A retry checks live authority again and never reuses a saved validity reply.
device_reconciliation.launch: On any launch paint immediately from the inventory left by the last completed reconciliation, within local expiry and after local signature and scope checks. Pending reconnect work has no first-paint dependency. Do not treat cached display as live authority. Remove anything already erased or pending durable erasure before prepaint. Fresh verified downloads and signed records accepted after reconciliation join that session's reconciled inventory. Before publishing staged acquisitions to this inventory, recheck their live authority under the current authenticated session.

relocate.rule: The same generic operation renames or moves any item within its checked space. Use the kind's ordinary placement and apply item_engine.title_binding for any declared dated-folder and on-disk title destinations. Maintain the reverse index of resolved Markdown destinations and the moved item's outbound relative links at write time. Follow both endpoints of relative links. Use the index to stage only the moved item and affected linking files, with inline and reference-style paths, URL encoding, visible labels and fragment anchors preserved according to the link contract. Stable item locators need no path rewrite. Charge the moved item and each inline rewrite against the applicable affected-file, staged-body-byte and link-edit limits. Use bounded index seeks with lookahead. Commit the placement even when link work exceeds any limit. Rewrite the work that fits inline and leave the rest to one durable host job. Neither the request nor the job scans the space.
relocate.commit: Resolve expected heads, checked destination and current authority for the move and host structural rewrites, including any disclosure and room fence. Use the existing per-space content writer and recoverable publication intent. Commit the placement, old-path binding, inline link bytes, backlinks, affected heads, span offsets, receipt, Undo intent and any rewrite job in one FULL transaction. Publish the new placement before acknowledging. Normal refusals for the moved item still apply. A busy linking file can be deferred without disclosing it. Undo is offered after completion and uses the same bounded operation in reverse, with the existing expected-revision fences. An old readable revision keeps its ordinary pin. Existing live executions keep the item identity and recheck the new head before writing. A cross-space move stays unavailable until an atomic implementation qualifies.
relocate.spans: Both a rename and a relative-link rebase change references through host-generated byte patches. Under the writer fence, shift or resize affected full, middle and quote ranges in every rewritten file and retain original attribution and live record identities. Record replacement bytes under item_spans.origins in every affected recorded span. Keep untouched bytes and existing discovery protection. Apply only patches that preserve record and attribution boundaries. Leave any ineligible link bytes intact with their stable resolution and report incomplete rewriting through the scoped status. Raw plugin replacements still use the opaque rule.
relocate.resolution: Reuse checked stable item locators and the indexed departed-path lookup. Commit the old path to stable item identity binding with the move, and retain the existing indexed target identities of the moved source's outbound relative links for rebasing. Resolve an already-bound link by its original target identity even if the old spelling is reused. Keep the binding while any indexed link still needs it and reserve the old spelling against ambiguous path reuse while path-only work is pending. Resolve to the current placement and preserve the fragment. Apply live source and target authority on every read and follow. Neither a stale path nor the status ref confers access.
relocate.deferred_rewrite: One receipt identifies one durable job for the remaining work. Resume from a durable index cursor. Commit each bounded batch and its progress together, with the current target placement and linking heads checked under the writer and room fences. Replan a changed head and skip a link that was removed or deliberately retargeted. A later relocation supersedes obsolete patches so a worker cannot restore an earlier destination. Apply current structural-edit authority and retain stable resolution until every eligible rewrite is published. Use bounded chunks and ordinary item size limits for work too large to stage inline. Never require a plugin wake.
relocate.status: Use the existing ActionOutcome and host.action.status. With no deferred work the outcome is ok. For a committed move with deferred work, pending and its status_ref describe only the rewrite job. The new path is already visible and the renderer can proceed. Return ok and any eligible Undo when all rewrites are durably published. A blocked job reports an error while the committed move and stable resolution remain in effect. Check live item authority and expose no hidden backlink counts, paths or identities.
relocate.qualification: On a perf VM under /usr/local/bin/perf-lock.sh, seed 100,000 mixed-authority items and run at least 100 relocations per arm with 0, 10, 64 and 1,000 backlinks in distinct files. Exercise file and folder rename and move, and hit the byte and edit caps independently. Time from request to durable commit acknowledgement at the new path and separately to all rewrites durably published. Report p50 and p95 for both, machine, runs, index reads, file writes, commits and flushes. Require commit p95 at most 40 ms with no backlinks and 100 ms in every other arm, with no regression against the running release on equivalent cases. In the overflow arms pause the job, follow every old-path link with live authority, restart after commit before ACK and during a rewrite batch, and verify one job, exactly-once effects, bounded foreground work and eventual publication of every eligible rewrite. Include path reuse, a changed linking head, rebased outbound links, Undo and preserved span attribution. No qualifying live result is recorded yet.

quotes.preserve: The destination quote pins the source item, exact source revision and span, and its original attribution. Keep those bindings with the stored quote bytes, independent of later source edits. Host relocation can rebase a Markdown destination inside the quote while preserving its label, wording and pinned source. On a non-delete replace_span, omission of quote keeps that checked block byte for byte and moves only its recorded offsets as needed. Recheck the existing quote's delivery authority without acquiring a fresh source span. A supplied ItemQuoteSource is an explicit re-quote and must pass the full check for a new quote. Redaction, including deletion of the enclosing reply, is the only way to remove a quote without replacing it with another checked quote.
quotes.compose: An attested record may carry one ItemQuoteSource. Resolve the exact currently available recorded middle at the checked source revision. Check live source body read, destination write and source access for the entire destination audience before commit and at delivery. Use no caller-supplied quote bytes. The host emits Markdown blockquote lines using > plus a space and a blank line after the block. The original middle bytes are kept in order. Track the emitted quote range and its source origin separately from the replying middle and plugin framing. Translate any source host byte ranges to the emitted quote so copied host-written bytes stay host-written. Quote bytes count against the ordinary record budget and the quote cap, independently of the framing cap. Refuse ineligible, empty or retired sources. Do not quote the source's framing or its quoted copies.

redaction.index: Use the same reverse-reference index as relocation, keyed here by the source item's durable record identity across edits. Store the exact quoted revision and destination record and byte range. Refuse a new live copy above copies_per_source across all destinations. Keep reverse dependencies for retained readable revisions and projections even after live rewrites. Refuse any write that would discard tracking of a live checked quote while leaving its bytes in the item. Checked cross-item quotes stay within the same space.
redaction.commit: Delete for everyone retires the original record under the expected-head and writer authority fences. Commit the tombstone, same-item quote removals, durable redaction fence, receipt and one resumable job for any remaining cross-item rewrites in the same FULL transaction before acknowledging. Serialize quote admission with the fence so no new copy can be admitted from a redacted record or its earlier revisions. Deleting a reply also removes any quote it contains and retires that copy in the same commit.
redaction.rewrite: Use the relocation rewrite job and its file, staged-byte and edit caps per batch. Seek by the source record in the index. Recheck the current destination head and checked copy under the writer and room fences. Patch only tracked quote bytes and commit the new head, span offsets, index and progress together. Preserve the reply, its anchor and surviving attribution. Assign host origin to generated bytes under item_spans.origins. Removed bytes have no origin at the new revision. Resume by durable cursor across restart and deduplicate by the delete receipt. Finish only when every live checked copy has been removed and the rewrites are durably published.
redaction.delivery: The redaction fence takes effect when deletion commits, independently of rewrite progress. Refuse body and range reads of any source or destination revision that still contains the redacted bytes. Clear its open body and view through the existing invalidations and suppress affected search matches, counts, excerpts, snapshots, caches and offline delivery. Unaffected records and independently authorized metadata may still be shown where they can be served safely. For an affected body with no safe projection, show the ordinary unavailable state until the cleaned head is ready. Then show the reply with no quoted block or deletion marker. Keep affected history unavailable until it can be projected safely. Reconcile offline copies at next authenticated contact. Retain the fence for as long as a source or dependent revision, projection or offline grant containing the redacted bytes can be served. The fence covers checked quotes, with arbitrary pasted text and exported copies outside its scope. Source grant loss or wider destination audience also fence dependent content before the change is visible, until redaction or authority is established.
redaction.qualification: Before enabling, exercise zero, one and 64 checked copies across mixed audiences, including same-item and cross-item copies from older source revisions. Refuse copy 65. Force multiple rewrite batches, pause after the fence and crash before delete ACK and after a batch commit. Require zero deleted bytes or derived matches on any authorized delivery path after the fence, no loss of neighboring text or span attribution, one job on replay, exact-once rewrites, and eventual removal of every checked copy. Include a racing new quote, a changed destination head, a lost grant and offline reconciliation. No live qualification is recorded here.

title_binding.rule: For a claimed-text kind, file_format.title_binding declares the only optional host-written title destinations. Install checks that the kind's ordinary title_field is writable, and that utc_date_folder has a visible kind root. The binding is data, with no format program or worker call. On create and on every title change, the host checks and applies the same title value to metadata, declared frontmatter and placement in the item writer transaction. Use item_engine.relocate for the resulting path change.
title_binding.placement: With utc_date_folder, the host adds one dedicated leaf folder named as the recorded item creation date in UTC (YYYY-MM-DD), a space, then the same normalized title stem used for an ordinary readable file name. Reserve 11 UTF-8 bytes for the date and separator, and space for any collision suffix, within the 120-byte component limit. Apply the ordinary collision checks. ItemCreate.name is the file name inside that folder and stays unchanged on rename. ItemCreate.folders and the rename folder operand are parent components above the generated folder. The generated folder counts against the four-component path bound. The creation date is held by the host and is unchanged by either rename or move.
title_binding.frontmatter: Bind one exact key in the initial --- delimited frontmatter. The checked body must contain exactly one unindented key followed by colon and space and a single-line literal UTF-8 title value. Require a nonempty trimmed title of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes without control characters and an exact match to the title metadata on create and saves that supply a body without a title change. For a title change, replace just the old value bytes under the expected-head fence. An accompanying save that supplies both body and title may supply the already-matching new value. This does not attest an otherwise opaque save. Missing or duplicate slots, an invalid value or incompatible span boundaries fail before publication. Patch the slot as host-made metadata and record its replacement bytes under item_spans.origins. It may occupy the whole recorded title middle and may not cross into another recorded range. Keep other recorded bytes, identities, quote bindings and attribution, shifting offsets as required.

format_open.rule: The owning kind declares file format identity and version, its installed default_app and any metadata_tokens. Check default_app against the owning plugin's installed apps. Open there by default. The person's explicit Open in choice may select an eligible editor contribution for the same format and version. Recheck current body authority and format compatibility for every open and write.
format_open.metadata: Only the owning format declaration specifies hideable tokens. A compatible alternate editor hides those tokens in the block view, preserves their exact stored bytes and anchors on a save, and retains access in raw view or export. Apply literal token rules only to their declared context. Frontmatter rules operate inside the initial frontmatter. Framing rules operate only on recorded framing, never on submitted middle or quote text. Author, timestamp, edit/delete and reply markers, and quotes stay visible unless the owning format explicitly declares other hideable metadata. Refuse a write if the alternate editor cannot preserve unedited metadata.

save_qualification.rule: For each save-gate workload take at least five independent runs on the locked perf VM. Compute p95 save ACK latency for each run. The median of candidate run p95s must be at most 40 ms and no slower than the median for the running release on the same workload and machine. Report every run and report save-to-ready lag separately.

attested_write.compose: Under the ordinary item writer and live authority fence, the host concatenates UTF-8 prefix, the optional checked quote block, the exact selected middle, and UTF-8 suffix in that order. Omitted framing is empty. Reject framing over framing_bytes_each by encoded byte length, and apply the ordinary body, append and frame bounds. Prefix and suffix are literal package-authored framing. Apply the owning package's declared reads and destination authority to them. Track their provenance separately from the middle. The separate quote rule governs its block. Copy the middle bytes unchanged. Refuse an ineligible source or span before publishing. Do not silently convert a refused attested write to an opaque write.
attested_write.placement: ItemAppend appends the single composed record at the checked head and ItemCreate can compose the initial body. Reject an empty record on either path. An empty create with no body adds no authored material. ItemSave with replace_span replaces exactly that one recorded span in the checked current revision. Apply quotes.preserve and quotes.redaction to its existing quote. Resolve the span with current item, package and write authority. Caller offsets are not accepted. For an edit use a newly captured input. For a delete use source kind empty, optionally with plugin framing for a tombstone, and apply quotes.redaction. ItemSave without replace_span accepts attested content only for a complete checked editor snapshot, with source kind input and empty framing. Its body is exactly the captured snapshot. An opaque body or stage uses the ordinary save path and cannot be paired with attested.
attested_write.record: Commit the new head, publication intent, body, protection state, receipt and span evidence in the same writer transaction. Record the entire nonempty composed span and its middle subrange, with package attribution for framing, captured actor or exact attempt for the middle, and source and revision binding. Return its ItemWriteSpanRef in the receipt. Replacements retire the prior span and leave unaffected spans addressable at the new head. A zero-byte replacement retires the span and issues no replacement ref. Whole-body writes retire all previous live span refs. Read committed spans through item_spans for as long as the exact revision is retained and readable. Retain recorded attribution with the revision, independent of receipt expiry, restart and package worker lifetime. Refs do not grant write authority and are not portable. Preserve ordinary historical revision and range pins. Exact replay returns the original receipt after live authorization with no repeated write or new evidence. Bind the fingerprint to the source, framing, quote source or its omission, entry anchor, target span and expected revision.
attested_write.opaque: Any opaque body write, including a raw append or a staged import at publication, makes the new head unproven and sets consent_only at commit. In the same commit invalidate all prior live spans, even if the old bytes still occur in the new body. The new revision starts with an empty span list. Old immutable revision entries stay readable only through the historical revision pin and never restore write eligibility. Later attested writes may record new ranges, with existing protection and the unproven body state preserved under the item discovery rule. A host-captured complete editor snapshot is the zero-framing case. A metadata-only save leaves body provenance and spans unchanged. Successfully composed framing is attributed to the package and does not, by itself, require setting consent_only.

item_create.scope: Owning kind and live create authority. Resolve the declared root, check readable placement, validate metadata and extractors, and commit file, head, readable path, publication intent and receipt together. Apply attested_write to the attested alternative and the item discovery policy to opaque writes.

item_head.scope: Check exact item and live read authority. Metadata follows its field authority. Require body-read authority for the head revision and byte length; refuse without body access.

item_range.scope: Check item, exact revision and live body authority on admission and delivery. Return bounded padded base64 and next_offset only when another range remains. Apply the existing range pin and purge rules.

item_spans.scope: Only a live declared read by the owning package. Recheck the acting principal and exact revision body-read authority at admission and at delivery, including any attempt fence. Use the item range pin, retention, purge and revoke rules. Refuse forged, expired or mismatched cursors and unavailable revisions. No returned ranges or attribution on a refusal.
item_spans.paging: Return at most the ItemSpansPage.spans maxItems, ordered by increasing absolute UTF-8 byte offset. Stop before the encoded worker frame cap. If a span has more host ranges than fit in one reply, return a nonempty chunk as the last entry with host_ranges_more and next. The next page starts with the same span and the next chunk. Every other span occurs once. Seek by span and range offsets with an opaque cursor bound to the package, acting principal, exact item and revision, and the same authorized read scope. Echo the item and revision and omit next at the end. Head advance cannot alter this revision’s pages. Distinct full spans are nonempty and nonoverlapping within their revision. The number of spans and host ranges is bounded by the body byte length. Span evidence expires with the retained revision. An attested empty body or an untouched opaque revision can return an empty page.
item_spans.origins: Use person for captured input by the acting account, attempt for checked output by the exact attempt, and host for bytes produced by title binding, link rewriting or redaction. For a wholly host-written nonempty middle or quote, use host as its attribution. Otherwise retain its default origin and use host_ranges for host-written subranges, including any in framing. Sort ranges by offset and merge adjacent host ranges. Ranges are positive, disjoint and within their full record, even across pages. Record the origin changes with the body and span offsets. Move surviving origins as offsets change, drop removed bytes, and leave untouched bytes and record refs attested. An empty middle has no attribution. Unchanged plugin framing keeps its existing treatment. Only the host assigns host origin. A plugin write cannot assert it or make an opaque body attested.
item_spans.boundaries: The full span, the exact middle and any quote must fit the checked revision bytes. The middle and the separately attributed quote are disjoint ranges within the full span. A heading-shaped line in the middle is ordinary submitted text. Use the recorded spans for boundaries when reading the body; do not escape, rewrite or infer delimiters from the middle. A tombstone with package framing has an empty middle. Historical span refs and attribution identify records only and cannot authorize edits, impersonation, consent or execution control.

item_save.scope: Check live item writer, expected head and receipt. Body or checked sealed stage replaces the body opaquely. Use attested for a recorded-span replace or a complete editor snapshot. Omit these operands for a metadata-only change. Apply patch to declared metadata. The owner can commit body, title metadata and a permitted relocation in one writer transaction, including intent and receipt. Apply relocate to any path change, including a leaf-only rename. Stale expected head yields head_conflict with the separately authorized current head. Reuse the room fence and preserve live checkpoints for metadata-only changes. Apply attested_write to the attested alternative and the item discovery policy to opaque writes.

item_save_begin.scope: Reserve the staged save under the existing receipt, body length and digest. Check writer and head. Keep both the checked begin identity and the checked final save identity in the committed receipt through receipt expiry, including after stage reclamation. Replay a committed save as ItemContentReceipt only for its exact begin or exact final save, respectively, under live authority. Changed operands conflict.

item_save_chunk.scope: Check scoped live handle. Accept bounded decoded base64 and check offsets and overlaps against the staged-save rule.

item_save_seal.scope: Check exact length and digest before sealing. The author passes staged to item_save; sealing publishes no item. Recheck expected head and authority at commit.

item_engine.placement: The kind declares the root. Apply item_engine.title_binding for a declared host-generated title folder. Name and optional child folders are checked single human-readable components, at most 120 UTF-8 bytes each after normalization. Reject traversal, symlinks, empty or platform-reserved names and path separators. Normalize under the host file writer's collision rules. Reserve each final path atomically with item creation, suffixing collisions deterministically as 2, 3 and so on. Probe at most 32 candidates, then refuse with path_conflict before publishing. Exact replay retains its reserved path. A folder is not an item ref or an authorization boundary. Use author-provided title/date and only an audience-checked actor_label from AuthorInvocationContext; neither account display name nor raw account ref is a default. The earliest slice can use title and date alone. Apply item_engine.relocate to every change of a published file or folder path.
item_engine.locators: ItemLocator is a stable space and item identity suitable for files, links and export. Resolve only through item.locate against current membership and item authority. Export keeps it as provenance; imports elsewhere use an explicit identity map if available. Never use it as a checked operand. Live ItemRef, HarnessRef, ChoiceRef, leases, receipts and provider session refs are not portable; regenerate or resolve them. App-owned stable message and participant IDs and a checked ContributionIdentity may be stored but confer no host authority.

created_outcome: A manifest operation with creates declares a closed output object with exactly one required field, created typed ItemRef. This declaration governs activation navigation. Internal own-item writes, including log files, use the declared item_create method without creates. Output maps to ActionOutcome.created only if the broker recorded that exact new item of the declared kind for this authenticated invocation, or an exact replay of it. Check live delivery authority before exposing the ref. Do not accept a foreign, old or unrecorded ref or a create claim from an undeclared operation. Dispatch then.route uses only the host-confirmed outcome.

group_people_scope.lookup: For participant lookup and grant admission, check live common group membership for the actor and every target in the checked group, before returning choices or committing item grants. Recheck at use. An account may belong to several groups. No server-wide participant lookup; protected administration is separate. A positive lookup grants no item authority.
group_people_scope.writes: Reuse the group membership and scoped invite primitives from ADRs 0058, 0059 and 0060. Under the afternoon decision, allow a live member to issue an invite scoped to their own group and provision a default shared space per group. Link issuance and redemption check the same live grant. Exact bootstrap replay identifies the same default space. Package-facing permissions and exchange details remain OPEN for Contacts.
group_people_scope.shared_item: Create one canonical item in the starter's space. Give selected participants full item privileges through checked item grants, within that item alone. Apply normal item fences, including item_audience_widening for reader additions and Undo. The app owns participant data, changes to the file and presentation. The host never treats that participant data as access proof.
group_people_scope.loss_of_common_group: When the checked participants no longer share any live group, preserve their existing item grants for read and export and make the shared item read-only for all participants. Keep its history. Refuse new messages, edits and disclosure calls to attempts. Recheck common-group membership under the write and disclosure fences. Apply attempt_authority_end.actions.grant_change to work that loses authority, including pending output, before the loss is published. Group departure alone does not erase the item or revoke its read grant. Ordinary account and item read fences still apply.
group_people_scope.open: The package-facing group, invitation, participant-grant and default-space exchanges are OPEN for Contacts, along with contact discovery and sharing UI. ADRs 0058, 0059, 0060 and 0064 govern the reused primitives; see the specification. Keep dependent package paths disabled until specified and qualified.

attempt_disclosure.rule: Disclosing authored material to an attempt requires live scope authority and consent from each author whose material is included. A checked explicit submission of the acting author's new text supplies that author's consent for that attempt. A package-authored author label or boolean is never proof.
attempt_disclosure.grant: An author chooses ask each time or always for the item. Ask each time yields a short-lived grant for the requested call. Always gives a long-lived author grant scoped to that item and eligible purpose, checked anew on each call. Either grant is revocable by its author at any time. Project the checked grants to the exact receiving attempt, selected ranges, immutable source revisions and approved purpose. Omit all material from authors without live consent, including those who have not answered. An item edit, share, Undo or read receipt cannot supply or restore another author's consent.
attempt_disclosure.delivery: Check the grants at admission and delivery under the attempt fence. On narrowing, expiry or revocation, apply attempt_authority_end.actions.grant_change to affected attempts and suppress queued disclosures and uncommitted output before further effects or delivery. Do not extend the selection to later appends or widen discovery through direct, indexed, derived, mounted or child access. A new invocation is required for a new selection. Consent adds no item grants or cross-space delivery authority.
attempt_disclosure.placement: Run with tools on for this selected-material invocation. In a personal space use the caller's own enrolled machine and approved login. In a shared space use the space binding under provider_login. Allow the invocation only after qualification proves that tools and unrelated runs cannot escape the selection or cross the applicable login and placement boundary. Refuse an ineligible placement. Do not silently use different credentials, widen discovery or launch with tools off.
attempt_disclosure.private_state: An app may keep private view state and consent preferences in a generic per-actor record scoped to the package and item. Authenticate the actor and recheck live item access. Other participants receive no projection or count of the record. A preference on its own confers no disclosure authority.
attempt_disclosure.consultation: If a caller requests a consultation, the app uses a separate linked item and the generic child-execution ceiling. A link confers no read rights or grant inheritance. Apply this rule to each receiving attempt before passing any selected material to it. The app may post the checked result to the original item, never the consultation exchange as a participant conversation.
attempt_disclosure.open: The trusted binding of checked entry selections to authors, grant issuance, expiry and revocation exchanges and checked placement remain OPEN. Until pinned and qualified, refuse this invocation into material including another person's messages.
